title: The VLT's Laser Guide Star
caption: The VLT's laser guide star under the southern Milky Way, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: A laser beam from the Very Large Telescope's 8.2-metre Yepun telescope crosses the southern sky. It creates an artificial star at 90 km altitude, high in Earth's mesosphere. The Milky Way, our galaxy seen edge-on, stretches across the whole picture.

Several other objects appear. The Carina Nebula is a bright patch to the left of the point the laser reaches. Between the two Unit Telescopes are, from the top down, the Large and then the Small Magellanic Cloud. On the right edge, just above a telescope, shines Canopus, which ranks second in brightness among all the stars in the sky.

The laser guide star is part of the VLT's adaptive optics system. It acts as a reference that lets the telescope correct its images for the blurring caused by the atmosphere, so astronomers can see finer detail than the turbulent air would otherwise allow.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken with a camera at an ESO site, in visible light. The camera settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long exposure gathers much more light than the eye, so the Milky Way, the Carina Nebula and the Magellanic Clouds appear brighter than they would to an observer.

explore: Julien Girard, an ESO photo ambassador, took this photograph, capturing the bright laser beam, two of the Unit Telescopes and the bright southern Milky Way together in one single frame.
alt: A laser beam rises between telescope buildings into a sky with the Milky Way, a bright nebula near the beam, two fuzzy galaxies and a bright star at the right edge.
